title: Precise length and charge segmentation of billion-dalton supramolecular polymers.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found the deposit (Northwestern ARCH repository, record w95051224, DOI 10.21985/n2-p91k-0v67) and listed every file by paging through all 8 listing pages: 54 Excel (.xlsx) files named after figure panels (Fig1C.xlsx ... figS92.xlsx), 5.67 MB total, licence Creative Commons CC0. Confirmed no structural depositions exist: EMDB (electron microscopy map archive) author search and a PDB (Protein Data Bank) search on the paper DOI both returned zero entries; Europe PMC reports no open-access full text, no supplementary files and no accession numbers.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about what is inside the files. Scripted download of the .xlsx files is blocked by an AWS WAF (web application firewall) JavaScript challenge returning HTTP 202 with a challenge page, so I never saw a single row or column. The science (living polymerization of peptide fibres, untwisted beta-sheet core, neurite outgrowth) comes from the abstract only; the accepted manuscript on the NSF public-access repository is embargoed until 1 October 2027.

a1_downloadable.note: Public and CC0, no login or application needed, so it passes on the checklist's terms. Caveat: a bot-protection challenge blocked my scripted download, so a human browser would be required to actually fetch the 54 files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The deposit is 54 per-figure-panel spreadsheets of plot source data (one file per panel, e.g. Fig2B.xlsx, figS33_heating.xlsx), not a feature/label table. Any prediction target (does a peptide self-cap, what segment length forms, does it grow neurites) would have to be constructed by hand from scattered panels and matched to molecules named only in the embargoed text.

a3_inputs_present.note: No molecule table: the peptide amphiphile sequences are described in the paper's methods, which is embargoed and not in PMC, so inputs would have to be transcribed from text or the supplement rather than read from a column.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verified either way; figure-source spreadsheets in this field usually carry axis labels with units, but I could not open any file to confirm.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on the modelling unit. This is a synthesis paper built around a handful of designed peptide amphiphile monomers; the spreadsheets hold spectra, scattering curves and microscopy measurements that are repeated readings of those few molecules, far under the ~1,500 labelled examples the checklist requires. Exact molecule count unverified because the methods are embargoed.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; size is the one thing that is not a problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No row counts to compare: the deposit advertises 5.67 MB and I counted 54 files, which is internally consistent, but the paper text is embargoed so no cross-check was possible.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists to trace. The underlying measurements are physical (microscopy, circular dichroism, X-ray scattering, calcium imaging), not model outputs, so circularity is not the issue here; A2 is.

existing_models.name: Transformer model for peptide self-assembly (aggregation propensity from coarse-grained molecular dynamics, >62,000 penta- to decapeptide samples)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors as ~6% error on aggregation-propensity prediction; split not checked (seen in search result summaries only, abstract not retrieved in full).

existing_models.name: AggNet (deep learning on ESM-2, a protein language model, plus AlphaFold2 structure features, for amyloid/aggregation prediction)
existing_models.score_and_split: Described by its authors as state-of-the-art on protein aggregation prediction; numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: Experiment-driven active learning for self-assembling pentapeptides (Science Advances 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; reported to discover non-intuitive beta-sheet-forming pentapeptides.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) would be the natural fit for peptide sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for a few dozen short peptides, but there is nothing to fit a head to.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; the deposit itself is CC0.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. Peptide self-assembly resources such as WaltzDB-2.0 (experimentally characterised amyloid hexapeptides) exist, but this deposit carries no peptide sequence column to join on.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: without a sequence-to-outcome table there is nothing to join.

controls.positive_control: None definable without a label table.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim can be written: the deposit contains plot source data for 54 figure panels describing a handful of designed molecules, not examples with a measured outcome.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use peptide sequence and assembly conditions to predict whether a molecule forms precisely length-controlled, charge-segmented fibres.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need one row per peptide amphiphile (a short peptide with a fatty tail that self-assembles into fibres) with its sequence and solution conditions. This paper supplies roughly a handful of such molecules, not a number I could verify, which is two to three orders of magnitude short.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the fibre self-caps at a controlled length, and what that length is, as measured by cryo-electron microscopy and light scattering in this lab.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Supramolecular chemists designing peptide fibres for nerve-regeneration materials would love a sequence-to-morphology predictor, but this paper cannot supply the training data for one.

more_or_better_data.why: Existing peptide self-assembly models trained on >62,000 simulated penta- to decapeptides and on experimental amyloid databases; this deposit offers figure panels for a handful of designed molecules.

confidence_score.why: Replicate measurements likely exist inside individual panels, but with no label table across molecules there is no per-prediction uncertainty to calibrate.

models_beatable.why: The named models are 2023-2026 and built on pretrained protein language models; nothing here could train a competitor, let alone beat them.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails every condition: no baseline can be run on these files, our model would see strictly less data, and no shared evaluation split exists.

ml_idea: The only idea the data supports is sequence-to-self-assembly prediction (peptide sequence in, fibre length and charge segmentation out). It dies immediately: the deposit is per-figure-panel spreadsheets for a few designed molecules, with the sequences themselves living only in an embargoed methods section.

effort.compute_note: Sizes read from the repository record (5.67 MB, 54 .xlsx files); no timing done because no feature table can be built.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct peptide molecules with a measured outcome. The file list alone answers it: 54 panel-specific spreadsheets, no molecule-level table, so the count is in the tens at best.

verdict_reason: Fails A2: the deposit is 54 per-figure-panel Excel files of plot source data, with no feature/label table and no sequence column; also fails A5 on scale (a handful of designed molecules) and A3, since the peptide sequences sit in an embargoed methods section. Downloads are additionally blocked to scripts by a bot-protection challenge, so I could not open a single file.
